newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Jan 27.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Inkatha Freedom Party secretary-general Ziba Jiyane and Gauteng legislature leader Musa Myeni handed in their resignations.
- Tough new measures are planned to crack down on insider trading, including proposals for more stringent laws and the introduction of a new system at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
- Building and construction group Shoredits was placed under provisional judicial management on Friday.

- For a fee of five rand, and a written undertaking not to use the information for commercial gain, the public will be able to gain access to the newly created public register of MPs' financial interests.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Stocks & Stocks, the construction group, is hiving off its hotel and leisure interests by offering institutional investors 110 million rand worth of shares.
- Private cargo carriers are challenging Transnet's restrictive regulations in the Durban Supreme Court.
- It appears there is more in the offing at Christo Wiese's fast-growing banking empire in the wake of the recent deal to bring Boland Bank and NBS Holdings into a closer association.
- The rand has appreciated against the dollar in the past two weeks because of the Reserve Bank intervention in the market, some analysts say.
SAKE BEELD
- Talks between the South African and European union took place over the weekend.
- Two important economic indidcators are due this week with the release of CPI and money supply.
- Shoredits Holdings, a construction group, was placed under judicial management on Friday.
THE STAR
- Cash-strapped councils throughout Gauteng face a crunch week as they juggle their books to pay creditors breathing down their necks.
- Negotiations over the Sandton rates boycott are in deadlock.
- Crowds clambered on to rooftops in Johannesburg's city centre yesterday to watch one of the world's master blasters flatten an entire block of buildings.
